title: Honoring the Ancestors
objective: After this level you can explain Chinese ancestor veneration and why families sweep graves at the Qingming festival.
summary: Chinese families have honored their ancestors since the Neolithic, with name tablets and incense at the home altar. At Qingming in early April, that care goes out to the grave.

cards.headline: Each spring, Chinese families go out to sweep their ancestors' tombs. Why?
cards.body: The festival is called Qingming. To understand it, don't start at the grave. Start at home, where the ancestors have a place every day.

cards.headline: The ancestors have a place at home
cards.body: Honoring ancestors in China is very old: it was deeply rooted by the Late Neolithic. Traditionally, the head of a household made sure offerings to the family's dead were constantly renewed. On the home altar, wooden tablets carry each ancestor's name with birth and death dates, and incense is offered there morning and evening. Picture a family tree you light incense for, twice a day.

cards.headline: A relationship that runs both ways
cards.body: Why keep it up, day after day? Ancestral spirits are believed to have the power to influence the lives of the living. Offerings honor them, and they are meant to turn away misfortune and bring good fortune. So veneration is more than remembering. It's a relationship: the family cares for its dead, and many believe the dead look after the family.

cards.headline: Clear and Bright
cards.body: Qingming means "Clear and Bright". It falls on the 15th day after the spring equinox, generally in early April, and is sometimes called Tomb Sweeping Day. Families clean their ancestors' tombs and leave offerings, burning incense, spirit money and paper models of valuable goods. The care the home altar gets every day, the grave gets once a year.

cards.headline: Honoring the Ancestors: the takeaways
learned: Chinese families honor ancestors with name tablets and incense at the home altar
Many believe ancestors and the living help each other
At Qingming, in early April, families sweep tombs and leave offerings

questions.prompt: What do Chinese families do at the Qingming festival?

options.label: Carry a portable shrine through the neighborhood streets
Clean their ancestors' tombs and leave offerings
Fast from sunrise to sunset for a month
